mainTopic: Oaths that cannot be taken, teachings of שמעון בן טרפון, the storekeeper's oath, and contradicting sets of witnesses
overview: The amud opens as רבה finishes his proof. The Torah frees heirs from an oath, which only makes sense if the father himself would have had to pay. The גמרא asks what רב and שמואל learn from that verse, and answers with שמעון בן טרפון's teaching that a false oath counts against both sides. Because his name came up, the גמרא adds three more of his teachings: a warning against helping an adulterer, the spies' complaining 'in God's tent,' and why the פרת is called 'great.' Then it returns to the משנה of the storekeeper and the workers. רבי questions the double oath, and רבי חייא answers from the משנה. רבא then shows that רבי agreed, since the workers swear to the employer in front of the storekeeper. Next, רב הונא and רב חסדא argue about two sets of witnesses who contradict each other. The גמרא maps out loan cases with two documents and leaves the case of two borrowers and one lender as תיקו. The amud ends as רב הונא בר יהודה begins an objection, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why would the Torah need to exempt the heirs?
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his proof. The verse only had to exempt the heirs because the father, in the same case, would have been obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if the father would be obligated in this case, because then the Torah needed a verse to free the heirs. But if the father were also free, why would we need a verse about the heirs?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his proof that a person who owes an oath but cannot swear must pay instead. His proof is that the Torah went out of its way to free the heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse that frees the heirs only makes sense if, without it, someone in that position would be obligated. So the father, who was the one who owed the oath, really would be obligated. That shows that when the oath cannot be taken, the obligation does not simply disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (the first half of an "if this, fine; but if that, why?" argument)
Why do I need it? (the verse would be unnecessary)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of the argument that an oath which cannot be taken turns into an obligation to pay.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that his father, in a case like this, is liable,
phrases.notes: "A case like this" means a case where an oath is owed but cannot be taken, so the person ends up paying.

phrases.english: then a verse was needed to exempt the heirs;
but if you say

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא נָמֵי פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: that his father, in a case like this, is also exempt,
why do I need a verse about the heirs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה's proof, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: A person who cannot take an oath he owes must pay.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse "שבועת ה' תהיה בין שניהם", which is read as freeing the heirs. That only makes sense if the father would have been obligated.

steps.title: What do רב and שמואל learn from the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב and שמואל, who reject רבה's view, use the verse "שבועת ה'".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב and שמואל: what do they learn from this verse, "שבועת ה'"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רב and שמואל, who do not hold that someone who cannot swear must pay. It asks what they do with this verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב and שמואל, the father and the heirs are the same, since neither one pays. So the verse is not needed to set the heirs apart. Every verse must teach something, so the גמרא asks what this one teaches according to them.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they learn from it?
"The oath of ה׳", the verse being discussed

phrases.english: And Rav and Shmuel, this verse "the oath of the Lord"
what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל – הַאי שְׁבֻעַת ה׳ מַאי קָא דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side reads the verse that רבה just used as his proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רב and שמואל learn from the verse, since they do not use it to free the heirs.

steps.title: The oath counts against both sides
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל use the verse for שמעון בן טרפון's teaching: a false oath counts against both people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what a ברייתא teaches. שמעון בן טרפון says: "The oath of ה׳ shall be between them both" teaches that the oath rests on both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב and שמואל use the verse for a different lesson, taught by שמעון בן טרפון in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "between them both" are read to mean that the responsibility for the oath falls on both people. That means the one who made the other swear and the one who swore falsely. Because the verse is busy teaching this, רב and שמואל do not need it to teach anything about heirs.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught in a baraita:
Shimon ben Tarfon says:
"The oath of the Lord shall be between them both"
teaches that the oath applies to both of them.
phrases.notes: He means that if the oath is false, both people share responsibility for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving the verse a different use.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse teaches that the oath rests on both sides, as שמעון בן טרפון says, and not that heirs are free.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה reads "בין שניהם" as freeing the heirs. רב and שמואל read it as teaching that the oath rests on both people.

steps.title: A warning against helping someone commit adultery
steps.stepSummary: Since שמעון בן טרפון was just mentioned, the גמרא brings another of his teachings: "לא תנאף" is also read as "לא תנאיף", do not cause adultery.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן טרפון says: Where do we find a warning against helping an adulterer? The verse says "Do not commit adultery," which can be read as "Do not cause adultery."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the main discussion for a moment. It quotes another teaching of שמעון בן טרפון, just because his name came up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "לא תנאף" (do not commit adultery) can also be read with different vowels as "לא תנאיף" (do not cause adultery). In this way the verse also forbids helping someone else do the act.

keyTerms.meaning: One who follows after, meaning helps, an adulterer

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching is not part of the argument about oaths. It is brought here only because the same חכם said it.

phrases.english: Shimon ben Tarfon says:
A warning for one who follows after an adulterer, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "Follows after" means helping him carry out the act.

phrases.english: The verse states: "You shall not commit adultery"
read it as: you shall not cause adultery.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַזְהָרָה לָעוֹקֵב אַחֵר נוֹאֵף, מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought in only because the same חכם was named in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a Torah warning against helping someone commit adultery, learned from reading "לא תנאף" as "לא תנאיף".

steps.title: The spies' murmuring was in God's tent
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן טרפון reads 'ותרגנו' as two words: 'you explored' and 'you disparaged', in the tent of the מקום.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you murmured in your tents.' שמעון בן טרפון says: you explored and you disparaged in the tent of the Omnipresent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues bringing teachings of שמעון בן טרפון. This one splits the word ותרגנו into two Hebrew words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ותרגנו is read as תרתם ('you explored', like the spies who toured the land) plus גניתם ('you disparaged'). The phrase 'your tents' is read as 'the tent of the מקום'. Their slander was done, so to speak, inside God's own home.

keyTerms.meaning: And you murmured, meaning you complained
You explored or toured the land
You disparaged, or spoke badly of it
The Omnipresent, a name for God

phrases.english: "And you murmured in your tents"
Shimon ben Tarfon says:
You explored and you disparaged
phrases.notes: He splits the one word ותרגנו into two: תרתם and גניתם.

phrases.english: in the tent of the Omnipresent.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: תַּרְתֶּם וְגִינִּיתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of שמעון בן טרפון, added because his name came up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ותרגנו = תרתם + גניתם, done in the tent of the מקום.

steps.title: Why the Euphrates is called the great river
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן טרפון explains that the פרת is called 'great' because it is close to ארץ ישראל: get near someone anointed and you get anointed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Up to the great river, the river Euphrates.' שמעון בן טרפון says: Come close to the one anointed with oil, and you become anointed.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching of שמעון בן טרפון. It explains why the תורה calls the פרת 'the great river'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרת is not the biggest river in the world. It earns the title 'great' because it is named next to ארץ ישראל. Closeness to something important passes greatness on.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is anointed with oil

phrases.english: "Up to the great river, the river Euphrates"
Shimon ben Tarfon says:
Come close to the anointed one, and become anointed.
phrases.notes: A popular saying. The פרת is 'great' because it sits next to ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further teaching in the same list from שמעון בן טרפון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Closeness to greatness makes something great.

steps.title: A king's servant is like a king
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teach the same idea with a different saying: a king's servant is treated like the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: A king's servant is like a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a matching saying from דבי רבי ישמעאל that says the same thing as the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the idea from the step before in new words. Whoever is attached to something great shares its importance. The פרת 'serves' ארץ ישראל, so it gets called great.

keyTerms.meaning: The study house (school) of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
A king's servant is like a king.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא: עֶבֶד מֶלֶךְ כְּמֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a matching version of the idea in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One attached to a great one shares his status.
steps.whatToRemember: This ends the list of שמעון בן טרפון's teachings. Next, the גמרא goes back to the משנה.

steps.title: רבי asks why both sides must swear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה of the storekeeper and his ledger. רבי asks why this double oath is needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the storekeeper on his ledger, etc.' It was taught: רבי said: Why the bother of this oath?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a storekeeper told to pay workers. It quotes רבי, who is unhappy with having both sides swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the storekeeper says he paid the workers and the workers say they were not paid. Both swear, and both collect from the employer. רבי asks why we need this trouble of both oaths.

phrases.english: And the storekeeper on his ledger, etc.
It was taught: Rebbi said:
Why the bother of this oath?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה after the side teachings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that both the storekeeper and the workers swear and collect from the employer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having both sides swear seems like an unneeded burden.

steps.title: רבי חייא: a משנה rules that both swear
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers רבי by quoting the משנה: both swear and collect from the employer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: We learned: Both of them swear and collect from the employer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רבי's question by pointing to the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא does not give a reason. He shows that the rule is already a taught משנה. Since it is taught, the double oath stands even if it seems like a bother.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to him:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, 'son of Abba.'

phrases.english: We learned:
Both of them swear and collect from the employer.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double oath is needless trouble.
steps.terutzMaskana: A משנה rules that both swear and collect from the employer.

steps.title: Did רבי accept this answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי accepted רבי חייא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he accept it from him, or did he not accept it from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about how the exchange ended. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never tells us how רבי reacted. The גמרא wants to know whether רבי dropped his question or kept his own view.

phrases.english: Did he accept it from him,
or did he not accept it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קִיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ אוֹ לָא קִיבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the outcome of the exchange between רבי and רבי חייא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי accepted רבי חייא's answer.

steps.title: Proof that רבי kept his own view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי saying the workers swear to the storekeeper. If he had accepted רבי חייא, he should have said they swear to the employer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי says: The workers swear to the storekeeper. And if it were so, he should have said 'to the employer'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to show רבי kept his own view. The next step pushes back on this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the משנה, the workers collect from the employer, so they would swear to him. רבי says they swear to the storekeeper. That shows he still placed the oath between the workers and the storekeeper, so he did not accept רבי חייא's answer.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Swear to the storekeeper' does not mean the storekeeper is the one swearing. It means the workers take the oath facing the storekeeper's claim.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught: Rebbi says:
The workers swear to the storekeeper.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי had accepted רבי חייא's answer.

phrases.english: he should have said 'to the employer'!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: פּוֹעֲלִין נִשְׁבָּעִין לַחֶנְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי did not accept רבי חייא's answer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי says the workers swear to the storekeeper, not to the employer.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's own ruling has the workers swear to the storekeeper. This suggests he kept his view against the double oath to the employer.

steps.title: Workers swear to the employer, in front of the storekeeper
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads רבי's words so that they fit with רבי חייא. The workers swear to the employer, but they do it in the storekeeper's presence, so they will be ashamed to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The workers take their oath to the employer, but in front of the storekeeper, so they will feel embarrassed to lie in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the proof from step 11. He shows that רבי's phrase 'swear to the storekeeper' does not have to mean רבי rejected רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא made it sound like the workers swear to the storekeeper, not to the employer. רבא says the oath really goes to the employer, which matches רבי חייא. 'To the storekeeper' just means the oath is taken in his presence. Because the storekeeper knows whether he paid them, the workers will be too ashamed to lie.

keyTerms.meaning: The employer (literally, the owner of the house)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end רבי and רבי חייא agree. Both sides swear and collect from the employer, and the workers swear in front of the storekeeper so they will not dare to lie.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The workers swear to the employer
in the presence of the storekeeper,
so that they will be embarrassed in front of him.
phrases.notes: The storekeeper knows whether he really paid them, so lying to his face is much harder.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: פּוֹעֲלִים נִשְׁבָּעִין לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof in step 11 by reading רבי's wording differently
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of wording: 'to the storekeeper' means 'in the storekeeper's presence'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי said the workers swear to the storekeeper, which suggests he rejected רבי חייא's view that both collect from the employer
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath goes to the employer and is taken in front of the storekeeper, so רבי agrees with רבי חייא

steps.title: Two contradicting sets of witnesses: רב הונא's view
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching is brought. When two sets of witnesses contradict each other, רב הונא says each set may still testify on its own in other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: About two sets of witnesses who contradict each other, רב הונא said that this set can come by itself and testify, and that set can come by itself and testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a related topic with איתמר. Here two sets of witnesses contradict each other, much like the storekeeper and the workers in our משנה. It brings רב הונא's ruling first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sets of witnesses contradict each other, one of them must be lying, but we cannot tell which. רב הונא says we cannot disqualify either set, because each one might be the honest one. So each set may still testify in future cases.

phrases.english: It was stated:
two sets of witnesses
that contradict each other,
Rav Huna said:
this one comes by itself and testifies,
phrases.notes: He means in some other case later on, without the other set.

phrases.english: and that one comes by itself and testifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי עֵדִים הַמַּכְחִישׁוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: two sides who contradict each other, as in the storekeeper case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two contradicting sets of witnesses are not disqualified; each may testify separately in future cases

steps.title: רב חסדא: do not rely on lying witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees with רב הונא. Since one of the sets is surely lying, neither set may be relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Why should I get involved with lying witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the opposite view. Neither set of witnesses can be trusted to testify again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא looked at each set on its own and said each one might be honest. רב חסדא looks at the situation as a whole: one of these sets is definitely lying. Since we cannot tell which, we should not accept testimony from either one.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Why do I need to deal with lying witnesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: בַּהֲדֵי סָהֲדֵי שַׁקָּרֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב הונא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both contradicting sets of witnesses are disqualified for future testimony

steps.title: Which loan case they argue about, and the one-lender case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where the dispute applies. With two lenders, two borrowers and two loan documents, רב הונא and רב חסדא argue. With one lender, one borrower and two documents, the holder of the documents gets only the smaller amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two lenders, two borrowers and two documents: this is where they argue. One lender, one borrower and two documents: the document holder is at the disadvantage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is mapping out cases. Each of the two sets of witnesses later signs a loan document, and the גמרא asks what happens to those documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two separate loans between different people, each document stands alone. רב הונא would accept both and רב חסדא would accept neither. With the same lender and borrower, one of the two documents must be false, since one of the sets is lying. So the lender may collect only the smaller amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The document holder has the lower hand, meaning he is at the disadvantage

steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses' contradiction happened in some earlier case. These cases are about documents that each set signed afterward, not about the original contradiction itself.

phrases.english: Two lenders and two borrowers
and two documents,
this is their dispute.
One lender, one borrower and two documents:
the holder of the document has the lower hand.
phrases.notes: He can only collect the smaller of the two amounts.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי מַלְוִין וּשְׁנֵי לוֹוִין וּשְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיְינוּ פְּלוּגְתַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case where the רב הונא and רב חסדא dispute applies, and gives a related case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about two separate loans. With one lender and one borrower, the lender collects only the smaller amount.

steps.title: Two lenders and one borrower match our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Two lenders with documents against a single borrower are just like our משנה, where both sides collect from the one employer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two lenders, one borrower and two documents: this is our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects one of the cases to the משנה of the storekeeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the storekeeper and the workers each have a claim that looks valid, and both collect from the one employer. In the same way, each lender holds a document that looks valid, so the single borrower must pay both of them.

phrases.english: Two lenders and one borrower
and two documents,
this is our משנה.
phrases.notes: Like the storekeeper and the workers, who both collect from the one employer.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי מַלְוִין וְלֹוֶה אֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיְינוּ מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues mapping the cases and ties one of them to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two lenders against one borrower follows the משנה: the borrower pays both

steps.title: What about two borrowers and one lender?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the last combination: one lender holding two documents, each against a different borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two borrowers, one lender and two documents: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the one case it has not yet settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each borrower can say, 'Maybe my document was signed by the lying set.' The question is whether each borrower may refuse to pay for this reason, or whether each must pay because his own document looks valid.

phrases.english: Two borrowers and one lender
and two documents: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי לוֹוִין וּמַלְוֶה אֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the remaining combination after the other cases were mapped
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether each borrower must pay the one lender, or may refuse because his document might be the false one

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the two-borrowers case undecided with תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without answering the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source or argument settles the two-borrowers case. So the question is left open with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: With two contradicting sets of witnesses, רב הונא accepts each set on its own and רב חסדא rejects both. Two lenders against one borrower is like our משנה. One lender against one borrower gets only the smaller amount. Two borrowers against one lender stays unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question in step 17 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of two borrowers and one lender with two documents remains unresolved

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה introduces an objection
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה announces that he is raising an objection from a ברייתא, opening a new challenge to the dispute about contradicting witness sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה raised an objection.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that רב הונא בר יהודה is about to challenge the earlier discussion, and the source he uses comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מתיב tells us a tannaitic source, usually a ברייתא, is about to be quoted against an אמורא's view. The open question so far was whether contradicting sets of witnesses can be relied on (רב הונא vs. רב חסדא). We have to wait for the next lines to see exactly which side the ברייתא seems to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה. This is the kind of source מתיב brings.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רב הונא בר יהודה with רב הונא, whose opinion was discussed in the previous steps. They are two different people.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda raises an objection:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיקו in step 18 closed the case breakdown, the גמרא turns to a challenge from a tannaitic source on the main dispute about contradicting witness sets.
steps.kashyaTarget: The dispute between רב הונא and רב חסדא about relying on two contradicting sets of witnesses (steps 13-14). The exact target becomes clear in the ברייתא that follows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, which carries the authority of the תנאים, will be quoted. If it rules against an אמורא's position, that position is in trouble. The details come in the next lines.
